nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number and let $H$ be a subgroup of a group $F$. Then $H$ is $p'$-isolated if, for every $x \in F$ and every natural number $n > 0$ that is not divisible by $p$, $x^n \in H$ implies $x \in H$.
nodes.title: $p'$-isolated subgroup

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number and let $H$ be a subgroup of a group $F$. Then $H$ is separable in the class of finite $p$-groups if for every $x \in F$ with $x \notin H$ there are a finite $p$-group $Q$ (a finite group in which every element $g$ satisfies $g^{p^k} = 1$ for some natural number $k$) and a group homomorphism $f \colon F \to Q$ with $f(x) \notin f(H)$.
nodes.title: Separability in the class of finite $p$-groups

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$ there are a set $\alpha$ and a finitely generated $p'$-isolated subgroup of the free group on $\alpha$ that is not separable in the class of finite $p$-groups. That is, the statement of Kourovka Problem 15.60 fails for every prime $p$.
nodes.title: Isolated subgroups of free groups need not be $p$-separable

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a prime $p$ such that, for every set $\alpha$, every finitely generated $p'$-isolated subgroup of the free group on $\alpha$ is separable in the class of finite $p$-groups.
nodes.title: Moldavanskiĭ's question on $p$-separability of isolated subgroups (Kourovka 15.60)
